solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Motto I'm going by as much as possible

indicators.note: going by here means passing alongside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: max, short for maximum, means the greatest amount possible
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone states their guiding principle: they always do as much as they can.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short saying expressing a rule of conduct, which is what a motto is.

clue.text: Some wiseacre moaning about posh car

indicators.note: about means the run of letters found is turned round
some of the words means only a stretch of their letters is used

explanation.surface: A know-all grumbles about someone's expensive car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes CREM from wiseaCRE Moaning and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merc is informal shorthand for a Mercedes, a luxury German motor.

clue.text: Cross with boy revealing picture

parts.note: a cross is the letter X in shape
Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed with a lad who has shown them a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray is a radiographic image, a picture of the inside of the body.

clue.text: Len wrongly connected with Madrid: he's from Birmingham?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a person from that region

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of the two words are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A man called Len is mistakenly linked with the Spanish capital when he is really a Brummie.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is England's second city, in the region known as the Midlands; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the central English region around Birmingham is a Midlander, so a Brummie is an example.

clue.text: Dried beef, cocoa, regularly, for girl

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A shopping list of dried beef and cocoa, oddly for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of DrIeD bEeF cOcOa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Was about to call newspaper's boss

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the past tense: surrounded

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone was on the point of phoning the editor of their paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was about' reads as 'was going to', but it means 'went round', as in a ring around something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have encircled something is to have been all around it, the sense of surrounding.

clue.text: Girl to live with Victor

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young woman is moving in with a man called Victor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bev, short for Beverley, is a female first name.

clue.text: Escort vessel my inspector endlessly provides

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a vetter is someone who checks or inspects

explanation.surface: An inspector, rather surprisingly, supplies a naval escort ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the R from VETTER to give VETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small warship used to escort convoys.

clue.text: Sailor about to mount challenge in S Wales town

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, to mount means the letters climb, reading upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a dare is a challenge

explanation.surface: A seaman is about to launch a challenge in a South Wales town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mount' turns RE upwards to ER in this down entry. Aberdare is a town in the South Wales valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a former mining town in the Cynon Valley in South Wales.

clue.text: African moved quickly, carrying stick

indicators.note: carrying means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: ran is to have moved quickly
a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: An African hurried along holding a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rwandan is a person from Rwanda, a country in central Africa.

clue.text: Poetry volume: the Queen's English

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A book of poetry described as the Queen's English.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing in metre, another word for poetry.

clue.text: Assume area staked out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone assumes a plot of land has been marked out with stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something without needing it proved is to presume or assume it.

clue.text: Having undergone revolutionary process after washing?

definitions.text: Having undergone revolutionary process after washing?

parts.words: Having undergone revolutionary process after washing?
parts.note: revolutionary hints at politics but means spinning round, as clothes do in a drum to remove water after a wash

explanation.surface: Something has gone through a revolution after a cleaning, like a country after a purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry dried by spinning in a drum has gone through a rotating process after being washed.

clue.text: Pen a poet ruined: say nothing!

definitions.note: an order to keep silent, matching an exclamation telling someone not to utter a sound

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet's pen has been spoilt, and someone is told to keep quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to stay completely silent, not making even the smallest sound.

clue.text: People who buy small jumpers

parts.note: hoppers are things that jump, such as grasshoppers

explanation.surface: Customers buying little sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like knitted pullovers, as British English calls them, but here means creatures that jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers in a store are those who purchase goods.

clue.text: In box, hid expensive leather

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone has hidden costly leather in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a bull or cow, tanned, is a type of leather.

clue.text: Victory, with time short, in season

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is missing

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A victory gained with little time to spare, during a particular season.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Cricketer losing heart becoming hero

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a batsman is a cricketer who bats

explanation.surface: A dispirited cricketer turns into a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The caped crusader of comics and films is a superhero.

clue.text: Characters with picnic baskets for Cockney and son

indicators.note: Cockneys, Londoners from the East End, drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: hampers are wicker baskets for picnics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picnic baskets packed for a Londoner and his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Cockney' drops the H of HAMPERS: Cockney is a working-class London accent that drops H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The & sign is a typographic character, and the clue's plural matches.

clue.text: Examination of the mouth

definitions.meaning: a spoken test, especially in a language exam
relating to the mouth, as in hygiene

explanation.surface: A dentist's check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a spoken test and anything relating to the mouth.

clue.text: Tense: description of border area?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, an adjective for a place on a border or rim

explanation.surface: An anxious frontier region.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nervous, and fancifully describes a place that is all margin.

clue.text: Yet these might be the odds

definitions.text: Yet these might be the odds

parts.words: Yet these might be the odds
parts.note: odd is the opposite of even, yet in betting an even-money price is a kind of odds

explanation.surface: A paradox: numbers that are the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a price where the stake is doubled if it wins is quoted as even money, a form of odds.

clue.text: Everything, or just part, for an audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: some means a part rather than the whole

explanation.surface: A speaker weighs presenting the whole or only a piece to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The total amount, as in 'the sum of it', is the whole lot.

clue.text: I dreamt about this hotel manager

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and scattered

explanation.surface: Someone recalls dreaming of the man who runs a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A head waiter, from French maître d'hôtel, oversees dining in a hotel.

clue.text: Job with island worker delivering letters

parts.note: a post is a job or position
Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Employment for someone on an island delivering mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries mail to homes is the mail carrier.

clue.text: In time, the Spanish slow down

indicators.note: in means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a day is a period of time
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Over time, Spaniards ease up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or make later is a synonym of slowing down.
